open_points.subject: A01 content identity ordering
open_points.text: “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)” does not break ties between edges with the same endpoints but different guards, or constants with the same destination but different values
open_points.question: How are tied edges and constants ordered before hashing, so equivalent submissions cannot receive different identities?
options: Add guard facts or the complete canonical edge to the edge sort key and constant facts to the constant sort key
Refuse duplicate edge endpoints and duplicate constant destinations during composition
Preserve submission order for ties, making it identity-significant
open_points.default_guess: Sort ties by the canonical JSON of the complete edge or constant.

open_points.subject: A04 authored trial cases
open_points.text: “its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports” does not say whether a present `expected_outputs` must contain exactly every output port
open_points.question: May an authored case specify only some expected outputs, and if so which outputs participate in `output_mismatch`?
options: Require exactly one expected value for every output port
Allow a subset and compare only the named outputs
Allow missing outputs but treat each missing output as a mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Require the complete output-port set whenever `expected_outputs` is present.

open_points.subject: K-02 and A03 filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input,” while A03 permits opening paths inside “one private exchange directory” and the read-only runtime
open_points.question: Which filesystem paths and operations may agent code itself use, as opposed to paths used only by the trusted runner?
options: Agent code may access the exchange directory and runtime
Only the trusted runner may access the exchange directory; agent code receives values and bytes only
Agent code may read the runtime but may access no exchange-directory paths directly
open_points.default_guess: Prevent agent code from opening any path; let only the trusted runner use the exchange directory.

open_points.subject: A03 clock isolation
open_points.text: The design says functions have “no clock” but the closed trap list omits standard-library clock sources such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.clock_gettime_ns`, `time.thread_time`, `time.thread_time_ns`, `os.times` and `resource.getrusage`
open_points.question: Are these omitted time sources allowed, or must they also be unavailable to function code?
options: Trap every omitted clock or elapsed-resource source
Allow the omitted sources and narrow the no-clock promise
Remove the closed list and enforce clock denial at the isolation boundary
open_points.default_guess: Trap the omitted time sources and treat any use as `sandbox_violation`.

open_points.subject: A03 deterministic execution
open_points.text: “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice” is required, but permitted Python can observe nondeterministic facts beyond the listed clock and randomness entry points, including process/resource information and object identities
open_points.question: Is deterministic output a guaranteed sandbox property, or only an expectation tested for selected implementations?
options: Guarantee determinism and close every observable nondeterministic source
Do not guarantee deterministic function output; define admission as deterministic only for the observations it actually records
Reject implementations that use a specified closed set of additional nondeterministic facilities
open_points.default_guess: Do not claim universal output determinism unless the isolation rules are strengthened enough to enforce it.

open_points.subject: A03 diagnostic output
open_points.text: “The output count is the sum” of returned value and file outputs, while “never stdout” is kept; no rule says whether stdout and stderr are drained, capped, redirected or counted
open_points.question: What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr?
options: Discard while enforcing a separate fixed byte ceiling
Count stdout and stderr against `output_bytes`
Redirect them to a bounded sink and classify overflow as `resource_exhausted`
open_points.default_guess: Drain both into a bounded discard sink and classify exceeding the bound as `resource_exhausted`.

open_points.subject: A08 binding port schemas
open_points.text: Proposal validation checks request shape and selected A02 port rules, but does not say that every binding `value_schema` must belong to the kernel's supported schema subset
open_points.question: Must an operation binding with an unsupported schema be refused at proposal time?
options: Refuse it as a manifest mismatch during proposal and acceptance
Keep it and let flow proof fail
Keep it and defer failure until invocation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it during proposal and acceptance.

open_points.subject: A08 manifest idempotency_key
open_points.text: “`null` means none; otherwise the text split on `+`” does not define an absent or non-string `idempotency_key`, especially for a `read` operation whose key is said to be copied “whatever those parts are”
open_points.question: How are missing, numeric, object, array or boolean `idempotency_key` values handled for read and non-read operations?
options: Treat missing as `null` and refuse every other non-string value
Require the field to be present and either null or a string
Ignore malformed values for reads but refuse them for non-reads
open_points.default_guess: Require the field to be present and either null or a string for every operation.

open_points.subject: A09 path-placeholder inputs
open_points.text: A proposal requires a placeholder input whose schema type is `string` or `integer`, but does not require `carriage: value` or `cardinality: one`; sending later requires “a non-null string or integer”
open_points.question: May a file input or a `many` input be bound to a path placeholder?
options: Require a `one` value input
Permit `many` and define how its list becomes one segment
Permit file inputs and define how bytes become a segment
open_points.default_guess: Require a `one` value input.

open_points.subject: A09 GET and DELETE inputs
open_points.text: Proposal validation examines each port's schema type, while runtime carriage for a `many` port is a list and query construction separately permits a list of scalars
open_points.question: How do port cardinality and schema type combine when deciding whether a GET or DELETE binding is valid, particularly for a `many` port whose element schema is itself `array` or `null`?
options: Validate the effective runtime shape after applying cardinality
Validate only the element schema and permit `many` only for scalar element schemas
Accept the binding and allow an unplaceable value to fail before sending
open_points.default_guess: Validate the effective runtime shape at proposal time and permit `many` only when each element has a supported scalar query representation.

open_points.subject: A08/A09 api_base_url
open_points.text: An instance URL need only be “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host,” while invocation removes a trailing slash and appends the declared path
open_points.question: Are user information, query, fragment, a non-root base path, encoded separators, IPv6 zone identifiers and other URL components allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the request and approval digest?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port with an empty path, query, fragment and user-info
Allow a base path and define RFC-based joining and canonical representation
Allow every absolute URL and concatenate strings exactly as written
open_points.default_guess: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, with no user-info, query, fragment or non-root path.

open_points.subject: A09 plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the `api_base_url` “host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: Is loopback determined from a literal IP in the URL, from DNS resolution, or from the actual connected address, and how are mixed or changing DNS answers handled?
options: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses qualify
Every resolved address must be loopback
The selected connected address alone must be loopback
open_points.default_guess: Only literal loopback IP addresses qualify.

open_points.subject: A09 multipart requests
open_points.text: Multipart bodies define their parts and deliberately omit the boundary from the approval description, but do not define boundary selection or the exact multipart byte serialization
open_points.question: What exact multipart encoding is sent, including boundary generation, CRLF placement, quoting and terminal delimiter?
options: Specify a deterministic canonical multipart encoding
Permit any standards-compliant encoding while approvals cover only the abstract part description
Use a pinned HTTP library's multipart encoding as release behavior
open_points.default_guess: Specify a deterministic canonical multipart encoding.

open_points.subject: A09 error-body credential filtering
open_points.text: For 3xx, 4xx and 5xx responses “reading stops at the ceiling,” but rule 7 says “the whole body is searched” for the credential before any part is kept
open_points.question: If an oversized error body contains the credential only after the read ceiling, must the detail be withheld, and how can that be determined without reading the whole body?
options: Search only the bounded prefix and say so
Stream-search the entire body while retaining at most the ceiling
Withhold every oversized error body without inspecting the remainder
open_points.default_guess: Withhold every oversized error body, avoiding an unbounded read.

open_points.subject: A07 and A09 failure_detail representation
open_points.text: An agent receives a protected `failure_detail` only as “its length and that class,” while HTTP error bodies may be arbitrary bytes and A20 truncates diagnostics “at a UTF-8 character boundary”
open_points.question: How is a non-UTF-8 error body converted to `failure_detail`, and is the disclosed length measured in source bytes, stored UTF-8 bytes or Unicode characters?
options: Store a defined UTF-8 replacement decoding and report stored UTF-8 byte length
Store bounded bytes and report byte length
Discard non-UTF-8 bodies and use a fixed diagnostic
open_points.default_guess: Store a defined UTF-8 replacement decoding and report its stored UTF-8 byte length.

open_points.subject: A07/A13 empty file-list disclosure class
open_points.text: An empty file list must retain a disclosure class and A07 says a file-list reference carries that class “even when empty,” but M23 represents file inputs and outputs only through SpooledFile facts, of which an empty list has none
open_points.question: Where is the disclosure class of an empty `many` file reference durably recorded so it can be recovered and disclosed after restart?
options: Add class metadata to every per-port file-list reference in NodeExecution
Create a separate stored file-list value record
Derive it from the node's inputs and port declarations whenever needed
open_points.default_guess: Record class metadata on the per-port file-list reference.

open_points.subject: A13 oversized mapped aggregate
open_points.text: A mapped value list above `stored_value_bytes_max` “fails the node for its dependants without changing any element's record,” while non-empty mapped nodes have no aggregate NodeExecution and the trace is the only source used to explain or continue a run
open_points.question: What durable fact records that the mapped node failed because its aggregate list was too large, and what exact conclusion/status is reconstructed after restart?
options: Write an aggregate NodeExecution with `contract_violation`
Add a separate immutable aggregate-failure record
Derive the failure from element outputs on every read and recovery
open_points.default_guess: Write a durable aggregate-failure record with reason `value_too_large`.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization order
open_points.text: “Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive” does not define arrival when requests are received concurrently by MCP or become readable together
open_points.question: What event establishes the total order of concurrent requests?
options: The MCP transport's accepted-message sequence
A sequence assigned atomically when parsing completes
An implementation-selected event-loop scheduling order
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically increasing sequence when a complete request message is accepted.

open_points.subject: A16 token-list reload
open_points.text: On an invalid re-read “the old list is not kept” and every request is refused “until a re-read passes,” but the text does not say whether failed bytes replace the remembered digest or what happens if the file later returns exactly to the last valid bytes
open_points.question: After a failed re-read, what state is cached and what condition forces later requests to parse the configuration again?
options: Enter an invalid state and re-read on every request until one succeeds
Cache the failed digest and re-read only when bytes change
Keep the last valid digest but discard its tokens, reparsing even when bytes match it
open_points.default_guess: Enter an invalid state and re-read on every request until validation succeeds.

open_points.subject: A20 release upgrades and admitted implementations
open_points.text: A release pins the sandbox runtime and dependencies, while earlier contracts keep only their resource bounds; nothing says whether existing admission verdicts and activations remain valid when a new release changes Python or sandbox behavior
open_points.question: After upgrading the kernel release, may an already admitted implementation continue serving without being admitted under the new runtime?
options: Keep verdicts and run the implementation under the new runtime
Invalidate verdicts and activations until re-admission under the new release
Retain and use the original release runtime for each existing implementation
open_points.default_guess: Require re-admission under the new runtime before the implementation can serve.
